gen-gf-margarine-mulish: Commanding and a bit showy, Margarine puts big-looking lowercase up front. Mulish follows with open, uniform strokes that make a long page of text feel easy and friendly.
gen-gf-margarine-poppins: Margarine turns heads with its oversized lowercase and smooth, plotter-drawn curves, while Poppins stays loose and sturdy beneath it. Bump the heading up a size.
gen-gf-margarine-rubik: Rubik is soft and clear, with round letters that hold up even when tiny. Rubik lets Margarine's pen-drawn, round-tipped shapes carry the personality while it handles the quiet work underneath.
gen-gf-marmelad-fs-literata: Marmelad has a faint swell of weight running through every curve. Literata answers with sturdy hairlines and open-mouthed curves, though a tiny heading would lose that subtle gradient against such a bookish body.
gen-gf-martel-fs-bespoke-sans: Bespoke Sans reads sharp and spacious, with curves that stay well clear of the stem. Martel adds a dignified serif voice above it, its g open at the bottom and its strokes lightly smudged like worn charcoal.
gen-gf-marvel-fs-literata: Contemporary and unfussy, Marvel links its wide-open letters like a short chain and never lets a hairline appear. Literata tapers mildly, like wire rolled barely flat, so paragraphs feel bookish and warm.
gen-gf-medievalsharp-bitter: Bitter reads dependable and grounded, its lowercase large and each s open enough to see through. MedievalSharp stands tall above it, bold and crisp.
gen-gf-medievalsharp-instrument-sans: Instrument Sans keeps one unbroken line weight throughout. Shrink MedievalSharp too far and its tall, wide-mouthed letters lose their commanding presence next to those open pincer-like c shapes.
gen-gf-medievalsharp-inter: Inter reads open and smooth, its tall lowercase breathing like a hollow reed cut lengthwise. MedievalSharp is best at making a bold entrance, while Inter is best at staying out of the way with signage-like plainness.
gen-gf-medievalsharp-mulish: MedievalSharp stands tall and bold, crisp even when shrunk. Mulish, drawn with compass-pencil consistency and horseshoe-open curves, keeps a long stretch of text approachable and easy going.
